bulgarian: You handle selling what you can via your $Shipping Bin$, and I'll take it from there!

english: It can be a challenge to get basic supplies out here in Mistria.
french: C'est parfois un vrai défi de mettre la main sur des denrées de base, ici, à Mistria.
russian: Здесь, в Мистрии, бывает трудно добыть даже товары первой необходимости.
bulgarian: It can be a challenge to get basic supplies out here in Mistria.

english: I can see why Eiland spends so much time out here. These ruins are quite impressive.
french: Je comprends pourquoi Eiland passe autant de temps ici. Ces ruines sont très impressionnantes.
russian: Понимаю, почему Эйланд так много времени здесь проводит. Эти руины действительно впечатляют.
bulgarian: I can see why Eiland spends so much time out here. These ruins are quite impressive.

english: I wasn't much for a winter beer, but it's grown on me thanks to Hemlock.
french: La bière d'hiver n'était pas dans mes habitudes, mais j'ai appris à l'apprécier grâce à Hemlock.
russian: Раньше я не очень любил пить пиво зимой, но Хемлоку удалось перебить привычку.
bulgarian: I wasn't much for a winter beer, but it's grown on me thanks to Hemlock.

english: Nothing better than winding down at the Inn after spending a day in the winter chill.
french: Rien de tel qu'un moment de détente à l'auberge après avoir passé la journée dans les frimas de l'hiver.
russian: Нет ничего лучше отдыха в трактире после долгого дня среди зимней изморози.
bulgarian: Nothing better than winding down at the Inn after spending a day in the winter chill.

english: I'd tell you what my wish is, but they say that's bad luck!
french: Je te dirais bien quel est mon vœu, mais on dit que ça porte malheur !
russian: Я бы рассказал тебе своё желание, но, говорят, не сбудется!
bulgarian: I'd tell you what my wish is, but they say that's bad luck!

english: I heard a rumor that there's a wishing well hidden out here by the Eastern Road, so I thought I'd have a look around.
french: Une rumeur raconte qu'il existe un puits presque invisible, exauçant les souhaits près de la route de l'est. Je me suis dit que j'allais le chercher.
russian: До меня дошёл слух, что где-то неподалёку от Восточной дороги скрывается колодец желаний. Так что я туда сходил.
bulgarian: I heard a rumor that there's a wishing well hidden out here by the Eastern Road, so I thought I'd have a look around.

english: Really?
french: Vraiment ?
russian: Правда?
bulgarian: Really?

english: Of course I'll go with you!
french: Bien sûr que je vais t'accompagner !
russian: Конечно я схожу с тобой!
bulgarian: Of course I'll go with you!

english: What's that? A bath... at the $Bathhouse$?
french: Comment ? Un bain... aux $bains$ ?
russian: Что такое? Принять ванну... в $купальне$?
bulgarian: What's that? A bath... at the $Bathhouse$?

english: I thought we could use some alone time, just the two of us...
french: Je me disais qu'on pourrait passer un peu de temps ensemble, rien que nous deux...
russian: Я подумал, нам с тобой не помешает побыть наедине...
bulgarian: I thought we could use some alone time, just the two of us...

english: Care to join me at the $Bathhouse$, [Ari]?
french: Ça te dirait de venir aux $bains$ avec moi, [Ari] ?
russian: Не хочешь присоединиться ко мне в $купальне$, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Care to join me at the $Bathhouse$, [Ari]?

english: Thank you for suggesting it, [Ari]!
french: Merci de ta proposition, [Ari].
russian:
Спасибо, что

предложили

предложилапредложилпредложило, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thank you for suggesting it, [Ari]!

english: I feel like a million tesserae!
french: Ça vaut tous les tesserae du monde !
russian: Чувствую себя на миллион тессер!
bulgarian: I feel like a million tesserae!

english: Ahhh... what a nice bath.
french: Ahhh... Quel bain agréable !
russian: Ах... какая приятная была ванна.
bulgarian: Ahhh... what a nice bath.

english: Going to the $Bathhouse$ with you is definitely the best way to unwind!
french: Aller aux $bains$ avec toi, c'est décidément le meilleur moyen de se détendre !
russian: Поход в $купальню$ с тобой вдвоём — определённо лучший способ развеяться!
bulgarian: Going to the $Bathhouse$ with you is definitely the best way to unwind!

english: That was great, [Ari].
french: C'était fantastique, [Ari] !
russian: Отлично сходили, [Ari].
bulgarian: That was great, [Ari].

english: Maybe down at the Beach?
french: Pourquoi pas sur la plage ?
russian: На пляж, может быть?
bulgarian: Maybe down at the Beach?

english: Great, let's go!
french: Super, en route !
russian: Отлично, пойдём!
bulgarian: Great, let's go!

english: Would you like to go for a walk, [Ari]?
french: Que dirais-tu d'aller faire une balade, [Ari] ?
russian: Хочешь сходить на прогулку, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Would you like to go for a walk, [Ari]?

english: Here, take my arm. Let's go!
french: Tiens, prends mon bras. Allons-y !
russian: Вот, возьми меня под руку. Пойдём!
bulgarian: Here, take my arm. Let's go!

english: Shall we go out to the Beach for a walk?
french: Si on allait se promener sur la plage ?
russian: Не прогуляться ли нам с тобой по пляжу?
bulgarian: Shall we go out to the Beach for a walk?

english: The way you looked with the sun on your skin and the sea breeze in your hair...
french: L'allure que tu avais avec l'éclat du soleil sur ta peau et la brise marine dans tes cheveux...
russian: Когда твоя кожа блестела на солнце, а волосы поднял морской бриз...
bulgarian: The way you looked with the sun on your skin and the sea breeze in your hair...

english: (Blush)
french: (Rougit)
russian: (Краснеет)
bulgarian: (Blush)

english: Well, you looked stunning!
french: Eh bien, tu étais <he>époustouflant</he><she>époustouflante</she><they>à couper le souffle</they> !
russian:
Ты

выглядели

выгляделавыгляделвыглядело просто потрясно!
bulgarian: Well, you looked stunning!

english: Well, I can't stop thinking about it!
french: Eh bien, je n'arrête pas d'y penser !
russian: Ну, я не могу перестать об этом думать!
bulgarian: Well, I can't stop thinking about it!

english: Thanks for joining me at the Beach, [Ari].
french: Merci de m'avoir accompagné à la plage, [Ari].
russian:
Спасибо, что

сходили

сходиласходилсходило со мной на пляж, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thanks for joining me at the Beach, [Ari].

english: Especially with you beside me.
french: Surtout quand tu es à mes côtés.
russian: Особенно, когда ты рядом.
bulgarian: Especially with you beside me.

english: A walk on the Beach is beautiful any time of year.
french: Une balade sur la plage, c'est magnifique toute l'année.
russian: Прогулка по пляжу прекрасна в любое время года.
bulgarian: A walk on the Beach is beautiful any time of year.

english: Hahaha!
french: Ha ha ha !
russian: Ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Hahaha!

english: Sorry, sorry...
french: Pardon, pardon...
russian: Прости, прости...
bulgarian: Sorry, sorry...

english: It's just... you're cute!
french: C'est juste que... C'est tellement mignon !
russian:
Просто... Ты

такие милые

такая милаятакой милыйтакое милое!
bulgarian: It's just... you're cute!

english: Of course I'll go with you.
french: Bien sûr que je vais t'accompagner.
russian: Конечно, я с тобой пойду.
bulgarian: Of course I'll go with you.

english: A picnic? Out in the $Deep Woods$?
french: Un pique-nique ? À $Boissombre$ ?
russian: Пикник? Прямо в $Глубокой чаще$?
bulgarian: A picnic? Out in the $Deep Woods$?

english: I had a really nice time on our last $Deep Woods$ picnic-
french: J'ai vraiment passé un bon moment lors de notre pique-nique à $Boissombre$...
russian: В прошлый раз мы отлично провели время на пикнике в $Глубокой чаще$...
bulgarian: I had a really nice time on our last $Deep Woods$ picnic-

english: Would you like to go on another one?
french: Ça te dirait qu'on en fasse un autre ?
russian: Хочешь устроить ещё один?
bulgarian: Would you like to go on another one?

english: I picked up some food from the Inn that we can share.
french: J'ai pris de quoi manger à l'auberge, on pourrait partager.
russian: Я взял в трактире еды на нас двоих.
bulgarian: I picked up some food from the Inn that we can share.

english: Hey [Ari]. I was wondering...
french: Dis, [Ari]. Je me demandais...
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Я тут подумал...
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]. I was wondering...

english: Would you like to go on another picnic?
french: Ça te dirait qu'on aille à nouveau pique-niquer ?
russian: Хочешь ещё раз сходить на пикник?
bulgarian: Would you like to go on another picnic?

english: I prepared everything myself.

french: Quand je le lui ai dit, il a essayé de me vendre un remède contre les maladies mortelles !
russian: Когда я ему это высказал, он захотел продать мне катапульту!
bulgarian: When I told him as much, he tried to sell me a catapult!

english: I trust Wheedle about as far as I can throw him.
french: Je me méfie de Wheedle comme de la peste.
russian: Я начну ему доверять, только когда заброшу его подальше!
bulgarian: I trust Wheedle about as far as I can throw him.

english: He's swindled many of them, usually in a manner so embarrassing that public accusation would make oneself look foolish.
french: Il a escroqué bon nombre d'entre eux, souvent de façon si embarrassante qu'en l'accusant publiquement, ils passeraient pour des imbéciles.
russian: Он многих облапошил, и обычно таким постыдным образом, что, если обвинить его публично, выставишь себя дураком.
bulgarian: He's swindled many of them, usually in a manner so embarrassing that public accusation would make oneself look foolish.

english: But nobles do gossip, so word gets around.
french: Mais les nobles parlent entre eux, alors la rumeur circule.
russian: Но слухи живут и у дворян, так что о нём узнают.
bulgarian: But nobles do gossip, so word gets around.

english: Wheedle is a bit of a menace to nobility in the Capital.
french: Wheedle représente une certaine menace pour la noblesse, à la capitale.
russian: Хлюст — почти что гроза столичной знати.
bulgarian: Wheedle is a bit of a menace to nobility in the Capital.

english: Nothing's scarier to him than rules and regulations.
french: Rien ne l'effraie plus que les lois et les règlements.
russian: Для него нет ничего страшнее правил и стандартов.
bulgarian: Nothing's scarier to him than rules and regulations.

english: Between you and me, Wheedle's a bit jumpy around Adeline.
french: De toi à moi, Wheedle est assez nerveux en présence d'Adeline.
russian: Замечу между нами: Хлюст перед Аделиной ужасно елозит.
bulgarian: Between you and me, Wheedle's a bit jumpy around Adeline.

english: These $Song Crystals$ could be huge, worldwide!
french: Ces $cristaux musicaux$ pourraient faire un tabac dans le monde entier !
russian: На её $поющие кристаллы$ найдётся спрос по всему свету!
bulgarian: These $Song Crystals$ could be huge, worldwide!

english: I wonder if Zorel would be open to a business partnership.
french: Je me demande si Zorel serait ouverte à un partenariat commercial.
russian: Интересно, Зорель ещё не думала найти себе делового партнёра?
bulgarian: I wonder if Zorel would be open to a business partnership.

english: I've done business with a lot of shady characters in my time. But even I won't cut a deal with Wheedle.
french: À une époque, j'ai traité avec pas mal de types louches. Mais même moi, je n'irais pas faire affaire avec Wheedle.
russian: Я многих мутных личностей повстречал за свою жизнь. Но даже я не стал бы заключать сделку с Хлюстом.
bulgarian: I've done business with a lot of shady characters in my time. But even I won't cut a deal with Wheedle.

english: I've never seen some of those gems before. I'm beguiled. Did they come from across the ocean? Where? I must know!
french: Je n'avais encore jamais vu certaines de ces pierres et j'en suis ébloui. Est-ce qu'elles viennent de l'autre côté de l'océan ? Mais d'où ? Il faut que je le sache !
russian: Некоторых самоцветов на нем я никогда не видел. Я заинтригован. Откуда они взялись? Из-за океана? Я должен знать!
bulgarian: I've never seen some of those gems before. I'm beguiled. Did they come from across the ocean? Where? I must know!

english: I tried to buy that =Alda Gem Bracelet= from the Museum, but Eiland and Errol absolutely refused.
french: J'ai voulu acheter le =bracelet précieux d'Alda= du musée, mais Eiland et Errol ont refusé tout net.
russian: Я хотел выкупить =альдийский драгоценный браслет= из музея, но Эйланд и Эррол напрочь отказали.
bulgarian: I tried to buy that =Alda Gem Bracelet= from the Museum, but Eiland and Errol absolutely refused.

english: It's a shame that they're so rare in Mistria's waters.
french: Quel dommage qu'elles soient si rares dans les eaux de Mistria.
russian: Жаль, что они нечастые гости в мистрийских водах.
bulgarian: It's a shame that they're so rare in Mistria's waters.

english: Still... I wonder if Terithia would ever want to run a little charter fishing operation?
french: Il n'empêche... Je me demande si Terithia aurait un jour envie de monter une affaire de sorties en mer.
russian: Но я всё-таки думаю... Может, Теризия согласится проводить небольшие рыболовные туры?
bulgarian: Still... I wonder if Terithia would ever want to run a little charter fishing operation?

english: Could be lucrative.
french: Ça pourrait rapporter gros.
russian: Тут может выйти прибыльное дело.
bulgarian: Could be lucrative.

english: Did you catch the $Amberjack$ that's at the Museum? Congrats!
french: C'est toi qui as attrapé la $sériole$ qui se trouve au musée ? Félicitations !
russian:
Я видел в музее $желтохвоста$. Это ты

поймали

поймалапоймалпоймало? Поздравляю!
bulgarian: Did you catch the $Amberjack$ that's at the Museum? Congrats!

english: That $Diamond Beetle$ at the Museum. What a beauty!
french: Ce $coléoptère diamantaire$, au musée, quelle beauté !
russian: Как этот $алмазный жук$ в музее. Какой красавец!
bulgarian: That $Diamond Beetle$ at the Museum. What a beauty!

english: Luc has finally convinced me. Insects can be pretty cool!
french: Luc m'a finalement convaincu. Les petites bêtes peuvent être assez sympas !
russian: Люку удалось меня убедить. Бывают очень крутые насекомые!
bulgarian: Luc has finally convinced me. Insects can be pretty cool!

english: It's a pretty antique. Aldarians know their jewelry, eh?
french: Il est assez ancien. Les Aldariens s'y connaissent en bijoux, hein ?
russian: Антикварная вещица. Альдарийцы знают толк в самоцветах, а?
bulgarian: It's a pretty antique. Aldarians know their jewelry, eh?

english: That =Family Crest Pendant= on display at the Museum! Your doing, no doubt.
french: Oh, ce =pendentif aux armes familiales= exposé au musée ! C'est à toi qu'on le doit, j'en suis sûr.
russian: Тот =Кулон с фамильным гербом= в музее — твоих рук дело, не иначе.
bulgarian: That =Family Crest Pendant= on display at the Museum! Your doing, no doubt.

english: The color, the translucence... like a beautiful, striated gem.
french: Colorée, translucide... on aurait dit une magnifique pierre précieuse nervurée.
russian: Какой цвет, какая прозрачность... Она похожа на чудный самоцвет с прожилками.
bulgarian: The color, the translucence... like a beautiful, striated gem.

english: Oh, I adored that $Giant Jellyfish$ at the Museum.
french: Oh, j'ai adoré la $méduse géante$, au musée.
russian: Ох, я в восторге от $гигантской медузы$ в музее.
bulgarian: Oh, I adored that $Giant Jellyfish$ at the Museum.

english: I like it!
french: Il me plaît bien !
russian: Мне очень нравится!
bulgarian: I like it!

english: That $Luminscent Crab$ in the Ruins collection... it's a bit of a show-off, isn't it? With the pink shell and the glowing and all...
french: Le $crabe luminescent$, dans la collection des ruines... Il est un peu tape-à-l'œil, non ? Avec sa carapace rose qui scintille...
russian: $Люминесцентный краб$ в коллекции из Руин... напоминает светского щёголя. Панцирь розовый, да ещё и светится...
bulgarian: That $Luminscent Crab$ in the Ruins collection... it's a bit of a show-off, isn't it? With the pink shell and the glowing and all...

english: It's simply magnificent!
french: Elle est tout simplement magnifique !
russian: Он просто великолепен!
bulgarian: It's simply magnificent!

english: I've never seen an emerald as flawless as that =Perfect Emerald= on show at the Museum.
french: Je n'avais jamais d'émeraude aussi parfaite que l'=émeraude pure= exposée au musée.
russian: Никогда раньше не видел изумруд такой же прекрасный, как музейный =идеальный изумруд=.
bulgarian: I've never seen an emerald as flawless as that =Perfect Emerald= on show at the Museum.

english: I'm all for archiving the world! I'd just love to archive that ruby right into my pocket.
french: Je suis tout à fait pour que l’on constitue des archives du monde ! Simplement, j'adorerais archiver ce rubis-là dans ma poche.
russian: Я только «за» сохранить для потомков хоть весь мир. Просто именно этот изумруд я бы хотел сохранить в своем кармане.
bulgarian: I'm all for archiving the world! I'd just love to archive that ruby right into my pocket.

english: I asked Errol if he'd part with that =Perfect Ruby= at the Museum, but he declined. Actually, he seemed a bit huffy about it.
french: J'ai demandé à Errol s'il accepterait de se séparer du =rubis pur= du musée, mais il a refusé. Il a même semblé un peu vexé par ma requête.
russian: Я спросил Эррола, готов ли он расстаться с =идеальным рубином= из музея, но он отказался. Причём как-то раздражённо.
bulgarian: I asked Errol if he'd part with that =Perfect Ruby= at the Museum, but he declined. Actually, he seemed a bit huffy about it.

english: Errol won't give me a permit for the Mines, but at least I can see every sparkling thing that comes out of it.
french: Errol me refuse l'accès aux mines, mais je peux au moins admirer tous les objets scintillants qu'on y extrait.
russian: Эррол не дает мне разрешения спускаться в шахты, но хотя бы так я могу посмотреть на все те блестяшки, что там находят.
bulgarian: Errol won't give me a permit for the Mines, but at least I can see every sparkling thing that comes out of it.

english: The =Perfect Sapphire= that was recently added to the Museum's collection! How enchanting.
french: Le =saphir pur= qui est récemment venu enrichir les collections du musée est un véritable enchantement !
russian: Тот =идеальный сапфир=, который недавно появился в музее, — просто очарование!
bulgarian: The =Perfect Sapphire= that was recently added to the Museum's collection! How enchanting.

english: Those $Ritual Beads$ in the Museum's collection are nice, aren't they? It's not my job to know what the ritual was, but I do appreciate a pretty thing.
french: Les $perles rituelles$ des collections du musée sont jolies, non ? N'étant pas spécialiste, j'ignore quel était ce rituel, mais j'apprécie les beaux objets.
russian: Те $ритуальные чётки$ из музейной коллекции хороши, правда? Мне не обязательно знать, для какого они ритуала, я просто люблю красивые вещи.
bulgarian: Those $Ritual Beads$ in the Museum's collection are nice, aren't they? It's not my job to know what the ritual was, but I do appreciate a pretty thing.

english: I thought Errol and Eiland would be more driven by scholarly curiosity. Me? I'm hoping for treasure.
french: J'aurais cru Errol et Eiland davantage poussés par la curiosité scientifique. Moi ? J'espère qu'il contient un trésor.
russian: Я думал, Эррол с Эйландом будут более любознательными. Я вот надеюсь на сокровища.
bulgarian: I thought Errol and Eiland would be more driven by scholarly curiosity. Me? I'm hoping for treasure.

english: Say, [Ari], could you have a word with Errol? He put that =Rusted Treasure Chest= out on the Museum floor, without even trying to open it!
french: Dis-moi, [Ari], tu pourrais glisser un mot à Errol ? Il a posé un =coffre au trésor rouillé= sur le sol du musée sans même chercher à l'ouvrir !
russian: Слушай, [Ari], можешь поговорить с Эрролом? Он выставил =ржавый сундук= прямо в музей, даже не попытался открыть!
bulgarian: Say, [Ari], could you have a word with Errol? He put that =Rusted Treasure Chest= out on the Museum floor, without even trying to open it!

english: Brilliant blue and a little showy. My kind of fish!
french: D'un bleu brillant un peu tape-à-l'œil, c'est tout à fait mon style !
russian: Ярко-синяя и немного хвастливая. В самый раз для меня!
bulgarian: Brilliant blue and a little showy. My kind of fish!

english: My favorite fish are the ones that look like gemstones, like that =Sapphire Betta= at the Museum.
french: Mes poissons préférés sont ceux qui ressemblent à des pierres précieuses, comme ce =combattant saphir=, au musée.
russian: Мои любимые рыбы — те, что похожи на драгоценности. Как тот =сапфировый петушок= в музее.
bulgarian: My favorite fish are the ones that look like gemstones, like that =Sapphire Betta= at the Museum.

english: That $Shardfin$ over at the Museum... it's a pretty thing, isn't it? Makes you think of fine jewelry.
french: Ce $guppy irisé$, là-bas au musée... il est joli, n'est-ce pas ? On dirait un bijou précieux.
russian: Этот $осколочник$ в музее... он ведь красивый, правда? Прямо как изысканное украшение.
bulgarian: That $Shardfin$ over at the Museum... it's a pretty thing, isn't it? Makes you think of fine jewelry.

english: Let's make sure it's a profitable one, eh?
french: Faisons en sorte qu'elle rapporte bien à tous les deux, hein ?
russian: Пускай оно у нас будет прибыльным!
bulgarian: Let's make sure it's a profitable one, eh?

english: A very good morning to you, [Ari].
french: Une belle bien journée à toi, [Ari].
russian: Добрейшего тебе утра, [Ari].
bulgarian: A very good morning to you, [Ari].

english: It certainly brightens my day!
french: Tes visites égaient ma journée !
russian: Мой день сразу становится лучше!
bulgarian: It certainly brightens my day!

english: I appreciate how you always check in to see how I'm doing, [Ari].
french: Ça me fait plaisir que tu passes souvent voir si tout va bien, [Ari].
russian: Спасибо тебе, что всегда интересуешься, как у меня дела, [Ari].
bulgarian: I appreciate how you always check in to see how I'm doing, [Ari].

english: I suppose that's part of its charm.
french: J'imagine que ça fait partie de son charme.
russian: Впрочем, в этом и есть часть её шарма.
bulgarian: I suppose that's part of its charm.

english: Mistria is always bustling, isn't it?
french: Il y a toujours de l'animation à Mistria, hein ?
russian: Мистрия всегда такая оживлённая, да?
bulgarian: Mistria is always bustling, isn't it?

english: I hope your day is going as well as mine is.
french: J'espère que ta journée se passe aussi bien que la mienne.
russian: Надеюсь, у тебя день проходит не хуже, чем у меня.
bulgarian: I hope your day is going as well as mine is.

english: Hey, [Ari]!
french: Hé, [Ari] !
russian: Привет, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]!

english: Let's keep the momentum up, [Ari]!
french: Ne perdons pas la cadence, [Ari] !
russian: Не будем сбавляем обороты, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Let's keep the momentum up, [Ari]!

english: Plenty of daylight left to make the most of.
french: Profitons bien du reste de la journée.
russian: Многое можно успеть, пока солнце ещё высоко.
bulgarian: Plenty of daylight left to make the most of.

english: [Ari], good afternoon!
french: [Ari], bon après-midi !
russian: [Ari], доброго тебе дня!
bulgarian: [Ari], good afternoon!

english: Something to look forward to for tomorrow!
french: Ça me motive pour la journée suivante !
russian: Поэтому мне всегда есть что делать завтра!
bulgarian: Something to look forward to for tomorrow!

english: It seems like the moment I have some downtime, I suddenly think of an exciting new business venture.
french: Dès que j'ai un peu le temps de me reposer, il me vient toujours des idées d'affaires à faire.
russian: Кажется, всегда, когда у меня находится свободное время, в голову приходит новая увлекательная бизнес-схема.
bulgarian: It seems like the moment I have some downtime, I suddenly think of an exciting new business venture.

english: Funny how things worked out.
french: C'est drôle ce que la vie nous réserve parfois.
russian: Забавно сложилась жизнь.
bulgarian: Funny how things worked out.

english: I didn't think spending time getting to know my clients would result in so many friendships.
french: Je n'imaginais pas que tous ces clients que je rencontre deviendraient des amis pour une bonne partie.
russian: Не ожидал, что знакомясь с клиентами, я заведу так много хороших друзей.
bulgarian: I didn't think spending time getting to know my clients would result in so many friendships.

english: And if not, let's spend some time together and I'll see if I can't lift your mood!
french: Si ça n'est pas le cas, passons un peu de temps ensemble, j'essaierai de te mettre de bonne humeur !
russian: А если нет, то побудь со мной немного. Посмотрим, может, я смогу поднять тебе настроение!
bulgarian: And if not, let's spend some time together and I'll see if I can't lift your mood!

english: Ah, [Ari]! Have a pleasant day, I hope?
french: Ah, [Ari] ! J'espère que tu passes une journée agréable ?
russian: А, [Ari]! Надеюсь, у тебя хороший день?
bulgarian: Ah, [Ari]! Have a pleasant day, I hope?

english: A very good morning to you, [Ari].
french: Une belle bien journée à toi, [Ari].
russian: Добрейшего тебе утра, [Ari].
bulgarian: A very good morning to you, [Ari].

english: It certainly brightens my day!
french: Tes visites égaient ma journée !
russian: Мой день сразу становится лучше!
bulgarian: It certainly brightens my day!

english: I appreciate how you always check in to see how I'm doing, [Ari].
french: Ça me fait plaisir que tu passes souvent voir si tout va bien, [Ari].
russian: Спасибо тебе, что всегда интересуешься, как у меня дела, [Ari].
bulgarian: I appreciate how you always check in to see how I'm doing, [Ari].

english: I suppose that's part of its charm.
french: J'imagine que ça fait partie de son charme.
russian: Впрочем, в этом и есть часть её шарма.
bulgarian: I suppose that's part of its charm.

english: In fact, I'd say it's part of your charm as well, [Ari].
french: D'ailleurs, ça fait aussi partie de ton charme, [Ari].
russian: И, кстати, часть твоего шарма тоже, [Ari].
bulgarian: In fact, I'd say it's part of your charm as well, [Ari].

english: Mistria is always bustling, isn't it?
french: Il y a toujours de l'animation à Mistria, hein ?
russian: Мистрия всегда такая оживлённая, да?
bulgarian: Mistria is always bustling, isn't it?

english: I hope your day is going as well as mine is.
french: J'espère que ta journée se passe aussi bien que la mienne.
russian: Надеюсь, у тебя день проходит не хуже, чем у меня.
bulgarian: I hope your day is going as well as mine is.

english: Hey, [Ari]!
french: Hé, [Ari] !
russian: Привет, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]!

english: If you have some free time, I'd love to take you on a date some time soon.
french: Si jamais tu as un peu de temps libre, j'aimerais bien qu'on fasse quelque chose ensemble, un de ces jours.
russian: Я бы хотел пригласить тебя на свидание на днях, если у тебя будет время.
bulgarian: If you have some free time, I'd love to take you on a date some time soon.

english: [Ari], good afternoon!
french: [Ari], bon après-midi !
russian: [Ari], доброго тебе дня!
bulgarian: [Ari], good afternoon!

english: But I look forward to every moment I can share with you.
french: Mais j'adore chaque instant passé avec toi.
russian: Но я ценю каждую минутку, которую удаётся провести с тобой.
bulgarian: But I look forward to every moment I can share with you.

english: I know neither of us has much downtime...
french: Je sais qui ni toi ni moi n'avons beaucoup de temps...
russian: Я знаю, что у нас обоих свободного времени немного...
bulgarian: I know neither of us has much downtime...

english: As always, I'm at your service.
french: Comme d'habitude, je suis à ton service.
russian: Я к твоим услугам, как всегда.
bulgarian: As always, I'm at your service.

english: Ah, [Ari].
french: Ah, [Ari].
russian: А, [Ari].
bulgarian: Ah, [Ari].

english: And if not, let's spend some time together and I'll see if I can't lift your mood!
french: Si ça n'est pas le cas, passons un peu de temps ensemble, j'essaierai de te mettre de bonne humeur !
russian: А если нет, то побудь со мной немного. Посмотрим, может, я смогу поднять тебе настроение!
bulgarian: And if not, let's spend some time together and I'll see if I can't lift your mood!

english: Ah, [Ari]! Have a pleasant day, I hope?
french: Ah, [Ari] ! J'espère que tu passes une journée agréable ?
russian: А, [Ari]! Надеюсь, у тебя хороший день?
bulgarian: Ah, [Ari]! Have a pleasant day, I hope?

english: I understand the feeling, I feel the same way when I'm spending time with you!
french: Je le comprends, je ressens la même chose quand je passe du temps en ta compagnie !
russian: И я его понимаю. Рядом с тобой я тоже наполняюсь счастьем!
bulgarian: I understand the feeling, I feel the same way when I'm spending time with you!

english: [child_0] always looks like he's having the best time when he's with you, [Ari].
french: Quand il est avec toi, [child_0] donne toujours l'impression de passer un très bon moment, [Ari].
russian: Когда [child_0] с тобой, он выглядит таким счастливым, [Ari].
bulgarian: [child_0] always looks like he's having the best time when he's with you, [Ari].

english: What adventures are you two up to today?
french: Quelles aventures vous mijotez, tous les deux, aujourd'hui ?
russian: Что у вас за приключения сегодня?
bulgarian: What adventures are you two up to today?

english: And here's my little family!
french: Et voilà ma petite famille !
russian: А вот и моя семейка!
bulgarian: And here's my little family!

english: I love spending time with him, but I don't think he finds some aspects of merchant life as interesting as I do!
french: J'adore passer du temps avec lui, mais certains aspects de la vie de commerçant n'ont pas l'air de l'intéresser autant qu'ils m'intéressent !

russian: Ах, [Ari].
bulgarian: Ah, [Ari].

english: With that big-eyed look of theirs, they'd certainly make a good merchant. Even I can't say no!
french: Ses grands yeux attendrissants en feraient un commerçant hors pair. Même moi, je n'arrive pas à lui dire non !
russian: С такими широченными глазами точно надо в торговцы. Никто не сможет отказать!
bulgarian: With that big-eyed look of theirs, they'd certainly make a good merchant. Even I can't say no!

english: [pet_name] was looking hungry, so I've already fed them.
french: [pet_name] semblait avoir faim, alors je lui ai déjà donné à manger.
russian: [pet_name] принимает такой голодный вид... Я просто не смог не дать еды.
bulgarian: [pet_name] was looking hungry, so I've already fed them.

english: They're quite the hard worker, aren't they? And so smart!
french: Mais c'est un animal qui travaille dur, n'est-ce pas ? Et d'une grande intelligence !
russian: Но [pet_name] так усердно и разумно работает! Возможно, я изменю своё мнение.
bulgarian: They're quite the hard worker, aren't they? And so smart!

english: I admit, I've never had a high opinion of pets before I met [pet_name].
french: Je dois avouer que je n'avais jamais tenu les animaux de compagnie en grande estime avant de rencontrer [pet_name].
russian: Признаюсь, я никогда не питал любви к домашним питомцам.
bulgarian: I admit, I've never had a high opinion of pets before I met [pet_name].

english: I'd prefer not to sleep in my wagon, but this tiny bed doesn't have enough room for both of us.
french: Je préférerais ne pas dormir dans mon chariot, mais ce lit minuscule ne peut vraiment pas nous accueillir tous les deux.
russian: Мне бы не хотелось спать в фургоне, но эта кроватка слишком тесна для двоих.
bulgarian: I'd prefer not to sleep in my wagon, but this tiny bed doesn't have enough room for both of us.

english: [Ari]... we need a bigger bed.
french: [Ari]... ll nous faut un plus grand lit.
russian: [Ari]... Нам нужна кровать пошире.
bulgarian: [Ari]... we need a bigger bed.

english: Seeing my things and yours combined... it's very cozy.
french: Tes affaires et les miennes mélangées... c'est très accueillant.
russian: Мои вещи вперемешку с твоими... создают чувство уюта.
bulgarian: Seeing my things and yours combined... it's very cozy.

english: Isn't the house looking nice?
french: Est-ce que la maison n'a pas fière allure ?
russian: Хорошо у нас дома, да?
bulgarian: Isn't the house looking nice?

english: I don't mean to be pushy, but I don't think it's a lot to ask either...
french: Je ne veux pas paraître insistant, mais ça devrait pouvoir se faire facilement...
russian: Не хочу тебе надоедать, но, по-моему, это небольшая просьба...
bulgarian: I don't mean to be pushy, but I don't think it's a lot to ask either...

english: Do you think we could make some room for my furniture somewhere in the house?
french: Crois-tu qu'on pourrait faire un peu de place pour mes meubles dans un coin de la maison ?
russian: Может, у нас получится найти в доме место для моей мебели?
bulgarian: Do you think we could make some room for my furniture somewhere in the house?

english: Time to make that dream a reality, eh?
french: Le moment est venu de faire de ce rêve une réalité, non ?
russian: Пора вставать и воплощать сон в реальность!
bulgarian: Time to make that dream a reality, eh?

english: I had a dream that I had so much coin in the bank, I had to open another account to hold all of it.
french: J'ai rêvé que j'avais tellement d'argent en banque que je devais ouvrir un deuxième compte pour que tout y tienne.
russian: Мне приснилось, что у меня было столько денег в банке, что пришлось открывать второй счёт, чтобы всё влезло.
bulgarian: I had a dream that I had so much coin in the bank, I had to open another account to hold all of it.

english: I'm looking forward to a relaxing night, how about you?
french: J'ai hâte de passer une soirée tranquille, et toi ?
russian: Я надеюсь сегодня вечером отдохнуть. А ты?
bulgarian: I'm looking forward to a relaxing night, how about you?

english: Good evening, [Ari]!
french: Bonsoir, [Ari] !
russian: Доброго вечера, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Good evening, [Ari]!

english: Come here, I've been looking forward to holding you in my arms all day.
french: Approche, j'ai attendu toute la journée de pouvoir te serrer dans mes bras.
russian: Иди сюда, я весь день хочу тебя обнять.
bulgarian: Come here, I've been looking forward to holding you in my arms all day.

english: There you are, [Ari].
french: Te voilà, [Ari].
russian: Вот ты где, [Ari].
bulgarian: There you are, [Ari].

english: You look like you've had an interesting day, I can't wait to hear all about it!
french: J'ai l'impression que tu as passé une journée intéressante, j'ai hâte que tu me racontes tout !
russian: По тебе видно, что день прошёл интересно. Жду твоего рассказа!
bulgarian: You look like you've had an interesting day, I can't wait to hear all about it!

english: Welcome home, [Ari].
french: Bienvenue à la maison, [Ari].
russian: С возвращением, [Ari].
bulgarian: Welcome home, [Ari].

english: I love you, [Ari].
french: Je t'aime, [Ari].
russian: Люблю тебя, [Ari].
bulgarian: I love you, [Ari].

english: Ah, there's the light of my life.
french: Ah, voici la lumière de mes jours.
russian: Ах, луч света в моей жизни!
bulgarian: Ah, there's the light of my life.

english: Maybe I can talk to Reina about making a snack out of whatever I have the most produce on hand to help entice picky folk.
french: Je devrais peut-être convaincre Reina de mettre au point un encas avec les produits de saison que j'ai en quantité, pour appâter les clients difficiles.
russian: Может, мне попросить Рейну готовить блюда из продуктов, которых у меня больше всего. Чтобы угодить разборчивым покупателям.
bulgarian: Maybe I can talk to Reina about making a snack out of whatever I have the most produce on hand to help entice picky folk.

english: I pride myself on anticipating a customer's needs, but you'd be surprised at how many ask for fresh spring vegetables in the middle of fall.
french: Je me targue d'anticiper les besoins de mes clients, mais tu n'as pas idée du nombre de gens qui veulent des légumes de printemps en plein automne.
russian: Я умею предугадывать желания клиентов и горжусь этим. Но ты удивишься, как много народу хотят свежих весенних овощей посреди осени.
bulgarian: I pride myself on anticipating a customer's needs, but you'd be surprised at how many ask for fresh spring vegetables in the middle of fall.

english: In the fall, there's deals everywhere you look if you're savvy.
french: En automne, il y a de bonnes affaires partout pour qui sait s'y prendre.
russian: Осенью для смекалистого торговца найти хорошую сделку не составит труда.
bulgarian: In the fall, there's deals everywhere you look if you're savvy.

english: Made some excellent deals today.
french: Les affaires ont très bien marché, aujourd'hui.
russian: Я сегодня заключил несколько превосходных сделок.
bulgarian: Made some excellent deals today.

english: Got to get a hustle on, there's all this fresh fall produce and only so many days to sell it!
french: Je dois m'activer, il y a plein de produits de saison tout frais, et pas énormément de temps pour les écouler !
russian: Мне надо спешить: столько свежих осенних продуктов, а дней на продажу осталось совсем немного!
bulgarian: Got to get a hustle on, there's all this fresh fall produce and only so many days to sell it!

english: You don't get days nearly as pretty in the Capital.
french: On n'a jamais d'aussi belles journées dans la capitale.
russian: В столице таких прелестных деньков просто не бывает.
bulgarian: You don't get days nearly as pretty in the Capital.

english: I feel like fall is when I first fell in love with Mistria.
french: Je crois que c'est en automne que je suis tombé amoureux de Mistria.
russian: По-моему, именно осенью я впервые влюбился в Мистрию.
bulgarian: I feel like fall is when I first fell in love with Mistria.

english: The day just feels full of possibilities, doesn't it?
french: La journée semble regorger de possibles, tu ne trouves pas ?
russian: Новый день полон возможностей, так ведь?
bulgarian: The day just feels full of possibilities, doesn't it?

english: [Ari], good morning!
french: Bonjour, [Ari] !
russian: [Ari], доброе утро!
bulgarian: [Ari], good morning!

english: It always feels like it's going to be a good day when I wake up with you next to me.
french: Je me dis toujours que la journée sera bonne quand je me réveille à tes côtés.
russian: Когда я просыпаюсь рядом с тобой, всегда чувствую, что день будет хороший.
bulgarian: It always feels like it's going to be a good day when I wake up with you next to me.

english: Good morning.
french: Bonjour.
russian: Доброе утро.
bulgarian: Good morning.

english: At least we can get warmed up together.
french: Au moins, nous pourrons nous réchauffer ensemble.
russian: Зато согреться можем вдвоём.
bulgarian: At least we can get warmed up together.

english: I'm soaked through from the rain, and I can see you're faring no better.
french: La pluie m'a trempé jusqu'aux os, et je vois que ce n'est pas mieux pour toi.
russian: Я весь вымок под дождём. Вижу, у тебя ситуация не лучше.
bulgarian: I'm soaked through from the rain, and I can see you're faring no better.

english: Now it just means I've got more time to spend with you!
french: Désormais, ça veut dire que je passe plus de temps avec toi !
russian: Теперь я знаю, что могу подольше побыть с тобой!
bulgarian: Now it just means I've got more time to spend with you!

english: Rain usually means a slow sales day. I used to mind more, but...
french: Quand il pleut, je ne vends généralement pas grand-chose. Ça m'ennuyait davantage, autrefois, mais...
russian: В дождливый день торговля обычно идёт не так бойко. Раньше меня это беспокоило, а теперь...
bulgarian: Rain usually means a slow sales day. I used to mind more, but...

english: Let's plan to head to bed early tonight, what do you say?
french: Allons nous coucher tôt, ce soir, qu'en dis-tu ?
russian: Давай сегодня ляжем спать пораньше. Как тебе идея?
bulgarian: Let's plan to head to bed early tonight, what do you say?

english: I've been overdoing it lately, seems it's finally caught up with me.
french: J'en ai fait un peu trop, ces derniers temps, je crois que la fatigue a fini par me rattraper.
russian: Я в последние дни засиживаюсь за работой. Кажется, усталость меня настигла.
bulgarian: I've been overdoing it lately, seems it's finally caught up with me.

english: Let's hibernate until spring.
french: Hibernons jusqu'au printemps.
russian: Давай устроим спячку до весны.
bulgarian: Let's hibernate until spring.

english: The only reason I could trudge through all that snow today was knowing that I was coming home to you.
french: La seule raison qui m'a permis de progresser péniblement dans toute cette neige, c'est de savoir que j'allais rentrer auprès de toi à la maison.
russian: Ты единственная причина, по которой я пробрался домой сквозь снег.
bulgarian: The only reason I could trudge through all that snow today was knowing that I was coming home to you.

english: I suppose we'd best head back to bed.
french: Je crois qu'on ferait mieux de retourner se coucher.
russian: Думаю, мы можем лечь обратно в постель.
bulgarian: I suppose we'd best head back to bed.

english: Plenty of snow fell in the night, and I don't think it's lightening up today...
french: Il a beaucoup neigé cette nuit, et je n'ai pas l'impression que ça va ralentir aujourd'hui...
russian: Ночью нападало много снега, и, кажется, он не думает останавливаться...
bulgarian: Plenty of snow fell in the night, and I don't think it's lightening up today...

english: Here's hoping it works out.
french: J'espère qu'elle va se concrétiser.
russian: Надеюсь, всё пройдёт гладко.
bulgarian: Here's hoping it works out.

english: I'm expecting an interesting business offer today.
french: J'attends une proposition intéressante, aujourd'hui.
russian: Сегодня я должен получить интересное деловое предложение.
bulgarian: I'm expecting an interesting business offer today.

english: Probably being held up by all that rain up north, spring thunderstorms are no joke.
french: Il a sans doute été retardé par toute la pluie qui est tombée, au nord. Les tempêtes de printemps sont redoutables.
russian: Наверное, задержался из-за дождей на севере. Весенние грозы — дело серьёзное.
bulgarian: Probably being held up by all that rain up north, spring thunderstorms are no joke.

english: Still no word of the cargo ship I'm expecting to arrive at the Capital.
french: Toujours aucune nouvelle du navire de marchandises qui doit arriver à la capitale.
russian: Я жду, когда в столицу прибудет грузовой корабль, но до сих пор никаких вестей.
bulgarian: Still no word of the cargo ship I'm expecting to arrive at the Capital.

english: Makes my job as a merchant that much easier, everyone has looser purse strings.
french: Cela simplifie beaucoup mon travail de commerçant, tout le monde délie plus facilement les cordons de sa bourse.
russian: Мне как торговцу это упрощает работу: кошельки раскрываются с лёгким сердцем.
bulgarian: Makes my job as a merchant that much easier, everyone has looser purse strings.

english: Everyone is in such a good mood in the spring.
french: Tout le monde est de si bonne humeur, au printemps.
russian: Весной все в приподнятом настроении.
bulgarian: Everyone is in such a good mood in the spring.

english: And mucky roads lead to late shipments.
french: Et qui dit routes boueuses, dit expéditions retardées.
russian: А размытая дорога означает задержки в поставках.
bulgarian: And mucky roads lead to late shipments.

english: Spring rains make for mucky roads.
french: Les pluies de printemps rendent les routes boueuses.
russian: Весенний дождь означает размытую дорогу.
bulgarian: Spring rains make for mucky roads.

english: I couldn't be happier!
french: Je ne pourrais pas être plus heureux !
russian: Как же я счастлив!
bulgarian: I couldn't be happier!

english: A beautiful spring day with you by my side.
french: Quelle magnifique journée de printemps à tes côtés !
russian: Ещё один прекрасный весенний день рядом с тобой.
bulgarian: A beautiful spring day with you by my side.

english: Everyone wants ice in the summer, but nobody wants to pay what it costs to transport.
french: En été, tout le monde veut de la glace, mais personne ne veut payer le prix de son transport.
russian: Летом всем нужен лёд, но никто не хочет платить за доставку.
bulgarian: Everyone wants ice in the summer, but nobody wants to pay what it costs to transport.

english: What a day.
french: Quelle journée !
russian: Ну и денёк!
bulgarian: What a day.

english: We'll sleep well tonight!
french: Nous allons bien dormir, ce soir !
russian: Сегодня хорошо поспим!
bulgarian: We'll sleep well tonight!

english: It's finally cooling down.
french: Ça se rafraîchit enfin.
russian: Наконец-то прохлада.
bulgarian: It's finally cooling down.

english: I really need to put an awning on my wagon one of these days.
french: Il faudrait vraiment que j'installe un auvent sur mon chariot, un de ces jours.
russian: Давно пора приделать к моему фургону козырёк.
bulgarian: I really need to put an awning on my wagon one of these days.

english: Looks like it's going to be another hot one...
french: On dirait que nous allons encore avoir une chaude journée...
russian: Кажется, день снова будет жаркий...
bulgarian: Looks like it's going to be another hot one...

english: If we have the chance, let's try to sneak out to the Beach together.
french: Si nous en avons l'occasion, essayons d'aller faire un tour à la plage ensemble.
russian: Давай выкроим время и выберемся вместе на пляж.
bulgarian: If we have the chance, let's try to sneak out to the Beach together.

english: This summer weather has been much too fine lately.
french: Cette météo estivale est vraiment trop agréable.
russian: В последнее время погода нас слишком балует.
bulgarian: This summer weather has been much too fine lately.

english: I need to get a thicker coat for these extra cold days...
french: Je dois trouver un manteau plus épais pour les journées particulièrement froides comme celle-ci...
russian: Мне надо прикупить тёплое пальто для таких морозных деньков...
bulgarian: I need to get a thicker coat for these extra cold days...

english: Nothing like a cozy house and a loving spouse after a long day out in the cold!
french: Rien de tel qu'une maison confortable et <he>un compagnon aimant</he><she>une compagne aimante</she><they>un·e partenaire aimant·e</they> après une longue journée passée dehors, dans le froid !
russian: Когда проведёшь день на морозе, так приятно, что дома уют и тебя всегда ждут!
bulgarian: Nothing like a cozy house and a loving spouse after a long day out in the cold!

english: They're a trial to take the wagon on in the winter, let me tell you.
french: C'est une véritable épreuve d'y déplacer le chariot en hiver, crois-moi.
russian: Фургон по ней тащить зимой — настоящее испытание, скажу я тебе.
bulgarian: They're a trial to take the wagon on in the winter, let me tell you.

english: I wish the road to the Capital was as well maintained as the ones here in Mistria.
french: Si seulement la route vers la capitale était aussi bien entretenue que celles que nous avons à Mistria.
russian: Вот бы дорога в столицу была такая жу ухоженнная, как в Мистрии!
bulgarian: I wish the road to the Capital was as well maintained as the ones here in Mistria.

english: In the Capital it'd already be gray slush by now!
french: À la capitale, elle se serait déjà transformée en boue grisâtre !
russian: В столице он бы уже давно превратился в серую слякоть!
bulgarian: In the Capital it'd already be gray slush by now!

english: Glad I'm out here with you instead.
french: Je suis content d'être ici avec toi, à la place.
russian: Хорошо, что я не там, а здесь, рядом с тобой.
bulgarian: Glad I'm out here with you instead.

english: Have you ever seen such pristine snow?
french: As-tu déjà vu une neige aussi immaculée ?
russian:
Ты когда-нибудь

видели

виделавиделвидело такой безупречный снег?
bulgarian: Have you ever seen such pristine snow?

english: It's so satisfying looking at the years of progress all neatly lined up.
french: C'est tellement satisfaisant de regarder toutes ces années de progression si nettement alignées.
russian: Приятно с годами замечать прогресс в аккуратных столбцах цифр.
bulgarian: It's so satisfying looking at the years of progress all neatly lined up.

english: Just reviewing my books.
french: Je parcours simplement mes livres de comptes.
russian: Просто перечитываю свои журналы.
bulgarian: Just reviewing my books.

english: Who knows if we'll end up playing it, but it's fun to write!
french: Je ne sais pas si nous aurons l'occasion d'y jouer, mais c'est amusant à écrire !
russian: Не знаю, будем ли мы в неё играть, но мне нравится сочинять сюжет!
bulgarian: Who knows if we'll end up playing it, but it's fun to write!

english: I had an idea for a Dungeon & Drama one-off.
french: J'ai eu une idée pour une soirée Dangers & Dragons exceptionnelle.
russian: У меня появилась идея на одноразовую встречу в «Перепалки & Драконы».
bulgarian: I had an idea for a Dungeon & Drama one-off.

english: just to keep my business senses sharp.
french: Tu n'imagines pas la concurrence féroce qui règne au sein de l'union aldarienne des marionnettistes !
russian: Так вот: ты даже не представляешь, какая в альдарийском союзе кукольников беспощадная конкуренция!
bulgarian: just to keep my business senses sharp.

english: Best I keep to what I know best, eh?
french: Mieux vaut rester dans un domaine que je maîtrise, hein ?
russian: Лучше уж я займусь тем, что знаю.
bulgarian: Best I keep to what I know best, eh?

english: I like to look into other lines of business now and then...
french: J'aime regarder de temps à autre ce qui se fait dans d'autres branches du commerce, juste pour rester à l'affût.
russian: Я люблю иногда заглядывать в незнакомые ниши, чтобы не ослаблять деловую хватку.
bulgarian: I like to look into other lines of business now and then...

english: I ought to get a chair like this for my wagon!
french: Je devrais installer un fauteuil comme ça, dans mon chariot !
russian: Надо бы завести такое кресло у меня в фургоне!
bulgarian: I ought to get a chair like this for my wagon!

english: It feels great to be off my feet.
french: Que c'est agréable de se poser un peu !
russian: Приятно, что можно наконец присесть.
bulgarian: It feels great to be off my feet.

english: I thought I'd give it a read first, but apparently the author insisted that it be printed in a language he handcrafted for the series.
french: J'avais pensé la lire d'abord, mais apparemment, l'auteur a insisté pour qu'elle soit imprimée dans une langue qu'il a lui-même créée spécialement.
russian: Я хотел сперва сам почитать, но, оказывается, автор настаивает, чтобы они печатались только на его специально придуманном языке.
bulgarian: I thought I'd give it a read first, but apparently the author insisted that it be printed in a language he handcrafted for the series.

english: I'll keep picking away at it, a good merchant needs to understand his merchandise.
french: Je vais continuer à la lire par petits bouts, un marchand doit comprendre les produits qu'il vend.
russian: Иногда я возобновляю попытки. Хороший торговец должен понимать, что у него за товар.
bulgarian: I'll keep picking away at it, a good merchant needs to understand his merchandise.

english: In this case, literally.
french: Dans ce cas particulier, c'est à prendre au sens littéral.
russian: А я буквально не понимаю.
bulgarian: In this case, literally.

english: There's a popular new book series from the Caldosian Empire called "Master of the Bracelets".
french: Il y a une nouvelle série de livres venus de l'Empire caldosien intitulée : « Le Maître des bracelets ».
russian: Сейчас появилась популярная серия книг из Кальдосийской империи, называется «Властитель браслетов».
bulgarian: There's a popular new book series from the Caldosian Empire called "Master of the Bracelets".

english: You'd be surprised how often Mistria gets mentioned these days!
french: Tu n'imagines pas le nombre de mentions de Mistria qu'on y trouve, désormais !

english: It takes practice...
french: Cela demande un peu d'entraînement...
russian: Для этого нужна практика...
bulgarian: It takes practice...

english: We can practice right now, if you want.
french: On peut s'entraîner tout de suite, si tu veux.
russian: Можем сейчас попрактиковаться, если хочешь.
bulgarian: We can practice right now, if you want.

english: I know the work is never done, but I hope you're taking time to sit back and enjoy the little things.
french: Je sais qu'il y a toujours à faire, mais j'espère que tu prends le temps de te poser et de profiter des petites choses.
russian: Я знаю, что работа есть всегда, но надеюсь, ты находишь время расслабиться и насладиться мелочами.
bulgarian: I know the work is never done, but I hope you're taking time to sit back and enjoy the little things.

english: Don't worry... I'll be home before you know it!
french: Ne t'inquiète pas... Je serai revenu en un rien de temps !
russian: Не волнуйся... Глазом не моргнёшь, как я вернусь!
bulgarian: Don't worry... I'll be home before you know it!

english: It's hard leaving for the city when you're here with me...
french: C'est difficile de partir pour la ville quand tu es là, avec moi...
russian: Так не хочется уезжать в город, когда ты тут со мной...
bulgarian: It's hard leaving for the city when you're here with me...

english: Warmer, these days.
french: Encore plus chaleureux, depuis quelque temps.
russian: Сейчас стало теплее.
bulgarian: Warmer, these days.

english: The Capital always felt cold to me, but Mistria is... warm.
french: La capitale m'a toujours paru froide, mais Mistria c'est... chaleureux.
russian: Столица всегда казалась мне холодной, а в Мистрии... тепло.
bulgarian: The Capital always felt cold to me, but Mistria is... warm.

english: Those things Wheedle said, about my past... they don't bother you, do they?
french: Toutes les choses que Wheedle a racontées, sur mon passé... ça ne te pose pas de problème, dis-moi ?
russian: То, что Хлюст говорил про моё прошлое... Тебе ведь это не важно?
bulgarian: Those things Wheedle said, about my past... they don't bother you, do they?

english: Not at all! But I am curious.
french: Absolument pas ! Mais cela attise ma curiosité.
russian: Вовсе нет! Но мне любопытно.
bulgarian: Not at all! But I am curious.

english: I believe in you! You can tell me when you're ready.
french: Je crois en toi ! Tu me diras tout quand tu seras prêt.
russian: Я в тебя верю! Ты можешь рассказать мне, когда будешь готов.
bulgarian: I believe in you! You can tell me when you're ready.

english: There was a bit of theft, a bit of espionage...
french: Il y a eu un peu de vols, un peu d'espionnage...
russian: Иногда были кражи, иногда шпионаж...
bulgarian: There was a bit of theft, a bit of espionage...

english: I thought I was maintaining some kind of moral code at first, but the deeper you get, the grayer it all becomes.
french: Au début, je me disais que je conservais une forme de code d'honneur, mais plus on s'enfonce, plus les zones grises sont nombreuses.
russian: Вначале я думал, что соблюдаю какие-то принципы, но чем глубже закапываешься, тем они серее.
bulgarian: I thought I was maintaining some kind of moral code at first, but the deeper you get, the grayer it all becomes.

english: I'm happy to have left that world behind.
french: Je suis heureux d'avoir laissé ce monde-là derrière moi.
russian: Я рад, что оставил этот мир позади.
bulgarian: I'm happy to have left that world behind.

english: I'm happier still that I'm here now, with you.
french: Et encore plus heureux d'être ici, désormais, avec toi.
russian: И я счастлив, что теперь я здесь, с тобой.
bulgarian: I'm happier still that I'm here now, with you.

english: Thank you, [Ari]. One of these days, I'll sit you down and tell you all about it.
french: Merci, [Ari]. Un de ces jours, je t'inviterai à t'asseoir et je te raconterai tout.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]. В один прекрасный день я сяду и всё тебе расскажу.
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]. One of these days, I'll sit you down and tell you all about it.

english: And maybe you can tell me all about your past, too.
french: Et peut-être que tu pourras me parler de ton passé, toi aussi.
russian: А может, и ты поведаешь мне о своём прошлом.
bulgarian: And maybe you can tell me all about your past, too.

english: I've been wondering, [Ari]...
french: Je me demandais, [Ari]....
russian: Меня кое-что беспокоит, [Ari]...
bulgarian: I've been wondering, [Ari]...

english: How do you go about making a place feel like a home?
french: Comment on fait pour qu'un lieu devienne vraiment son chez-soi ?
russian: Что нужно сделать, чтобы место ощущалось как дом?
bulgarian: How do you go about making a place feel like a home?

english: Add some touches that reflect your interests!
french: Ajoute quelques touches qui reflètent tes centres d'intérêt !
russian: Добавь что-то, что отражает твои увлечения!
bulgarian: Add some touches that reflect your interests!

english: Add something that makes you feel happy!
french: Ajoute quelque chose qui te rend heureux !
russian: Добавь что-то, что приносит радость!
bulgarian: Add something that makes you feel happy!

english: Perhaps a wine rack? A gemstone case?
french: Un casier à bouteilles, peut-être ? Une boîte à pierres précieuses ?
russian: Может, полку с винами? Или витрину с драгоценностями?
bulgarian: Perhaps a wine rack? A gemstone case?

english: Hmmm... I'm not sure.
french: Mmm... Je ne sais pas trop.
russian: Хммм... не уверен.
bulgarian: Hmmm... I'm not sure.

english: Maybe you can come over some time and help me decide?
french: Peut-être que tu pourrais passer, à l'occasion, pour m'aider à choisir ?
russian: Может, ты как-нибудь зайдёшь и поможешь мне выбрать?
bulgarian: Maybe you can come over some time and help me decide?

english: Something that makes me feel happy...?
french: Quelque chose qui me rend heureux...?
russian: Что приносит мне радость?..
bulgarian: Something that makes me feel happy...?

english: Well in that case... Maybe you can come over some time?
french: Eh bien, dans ce cas... Peut-être que tu pourrais passer, à l'occasion ?
russian: Что ж, в таком случае... Может, ты как-нибудь зайдёшь?
bulgarian: Well in that case... Maybe you can come over some time?

english: I've been trying to make my room at the Inn feel more welcoming... the kind of place you'd want to visit.
french: J'essaie de rendre ma chambre à l'auberge un peu plus accueillante... Que ce soit un endroit où on aime se rendre.
russian: Я стараюсь добавить уюта в свою комнату в трактире... чтобы туда хотелось приходить.
bulgarian: I've been trying to make my room at the Inn feel more welcoming... the kind of place you'd want to visit.

english: For so much of my life, it felt safer to keep others at arm's length.
french: Pendant une grande partie de ma vie, cela m'a semblé plus sûr de tenir les autres à distance.
russian: Почти всю мою жизнь я чувствовал себя безопаснее, когда держал людей на расстоянии.
bulgarian: For so much of my life, it felt safer to keep others at arm's length.

english: Sometimes I feel out of sorts if I'm not putting on my merchant's charm.
french: Je me sens parfois mal à l'aise si je ne joue pas mon rôle de marchand charmeur.
russian: Иногда я чувствую себя будто не в своей тарелке, когда отбрасываю повадки торговца.
bulgarian: Sometimes I feel out of sorts if I'm not putting on my merchant's charm.

english: I hope you'll forgive me if it still slips through now and then.
french: J'espère que tu me pardonneras si ce personnage réapparaît de temps à autre.
russian: Надеюсь, ты меня простишь, если они иногда всё же проскользнут.
bulgarian: I hope you'll forgive me if it still slips through now and then.

english: I don't mind, I think it's cute!
french: Ce n'est pas grave, je trouve ça charmant !
russian: Я не против. По-моему, это мило!
bulgarian: I don't mind, I think it's cute!

english: I'm enjoying this new side of you!
french: J'aime beaucoup ce nouvel aspect de ta personnalité !
russian: Мне нравится узнавать тебя с новой стороны!
bulgarian: I'm enjoying this new side of you!

english: Oh! Y-you do?
french: Oh ! V-Vraiment ?
russian: Ой! П-правда?
bulgarian: Oh! Y-you do?

english: Thank you, [Ari].
french: Merci, [Ari].
russian: Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari].

english: I'm glad you feel that way.
french: Ça me fait plaisir que tu ressentes ça.
russian: Я рад, что ты так считаешь.
bulgarian: I'm glad you feel that way.

english: It's hard work sometimes, I won't lie.
french: Je ne vais pas te mentir, ça me demande parfois beaucoup d'efforts.
russian: Лгать не буду, иногда бывает тяжело.
bulgarian: It's hard work sometimes, I won't lie.

english: But, well... I suppose neither of us are strangers to hard work.
french: Mais bon... J'imagine que les efforts, on connaît ça, toi et moi.
russian: Но вообще-то... Мы с тобой ведь не боимся тяжёлой работы.
bulgarian: But, well... I suppose neither of us are strangers to hard work.

english: It's a strange feeling... really opening up to another person.
french: C'est un sentiment étrange... de s'ouvrir réellement à quelqu'un d'autre.
russian: Такое странное чувство... Открывать душу другому человеку.
bulgarian: It's a strange feeling... really opening up to another person.

english: This morning he asked if I'd ever consider becoming a farmer!
french: Ce matin, il m'a demandé si j'avais déjà envisagé de devenir fermier !
russian: Сегодня утром он спросил, не думал ли я стать фермером!
bulgarian: This morning he asked if I'd ever consider becoming a farmer!

english: What do you think, [Ari]? Do I have what it takes?
french: Qu'en penses-tu, [Ari] ? Tu crois que j'en serais capable ?
russian: Как думаешь, [Ari]? У меня бы получилось?
bulgarian: What do you think, [Ari]? Do I have what it takes?

english: Do you want to be a farmer?
french: As-tu envie de travailler dans une ferme ?
russian: А ты сам хочешь быть фермером?
bulgarian: Do you want to be a farmer?

english: You're better off dating a farmer than becoming one yourself.
french: Mieux vaut sortir avec quelqu'un qui a une ferme qu'y travailler soi-même.
russian: Лучше пускай у тебя будет партнёр-фермер.
bulgarian: You're better off dating a farmer than becoming one yourself.

english: Oh, I don't know...
french: Oh, je ne sais pas...
russian: Ой, я не знаю...
bulgarian: Oh, I don't know...

english: Toiling side by side, sweating and laughing under the hot sun...
french: Trimer côte à côte, transpirer et rire sous la chaleur du soleil...
russian: Трудиться вместе с тобой, работать в поту и смеяться под палящим солнцем...
bulgarian: Toiling side by side, sweating and laughing under the hot sun...

english: There is something romantic about the idea.
french: L'idée a quelque chose de romantique.
russian: В этом есть что-то романтичное.
bulgarian: There is something romantic about the idea.

english: Just, um... don't tell Hemlock I said that, okay?
french: Seulement, hum... Ne va pas raconter ça à Hemlock, d'accord ?
russian: Только, эмм... не говори Хемлоку, что я это сказал, ладно?
bulgarian: Just, um... don't tell Hemlock I said that, okay?

english: Hmmm... you don't say.
french: Mmm... Je ne te le fais pas dire.
russian: Хммм... Неужели?
bulgarian: Hmmm... you don't say.

english: Yeah, I guess that does sound more my speed.
french: Oui, je crois que ça me convient mieux.
russian: Да, наверное, это мне больше по плечу.
bulgarian: Yeah, I guess that does sound more my speed.

english: You know, Hemlock's started teasing me a bit lately.
french: Tu sais, Hemlock s'est mis à se moquer un peu de moi, dernièrement.
russian: Знаешь, недавно Хемлок стал меня дразнить.
bulgarian: You know, Hemlock's started teasing me a bit lately.
